China, facing a 20% tariff that could double to 40%, rejected allegations of overcapacity and reserved the right to retaliate. ... The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has reached 12,021 confirmed cases and 5,904 deaths, according to government data released on Thursday. The outbreak, which began in May in the northeastern province of Ituri, has spread to eight of the country’s 26 provinces. It is the fastest growing Ebola outbreak on record. Renewed fighting between government forces and rebels has disrupted efforts to contain the disease. World Health Organization Ebola incident manager Dr Catherine Smallwood said fighting had prevented response teams from reaching some communities, disrupted contact tracing and reduced staffing at treatment centres. Health officials and WHO personnel have also been evacuated.

items.title: Energy Prices Cooled But Core Inflation Stayed Hot | The Daily Economy
items.excerpt: Bryan Cutsinger November 27, 2026 Rising energy prices have accounted for much of the increase in inflation this year. But despite a relatively modest increase in energy prices in October, inflation remains well above the Federal Reserve’s 2-percent target. Annual core inflation has increased, and nominal spending is growing even faster than previously estimated. Taken together, these figures make the case for another rate increase in December. The Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) reported on Wednesday that the Personal Consumption Expenditures Price Index (PCEPI), the Fed’s preferred measure of inflation, rose 0.3 percent in October, compared with 0.5 percent in September. Over the past six months, prices have risen at an annualized rate of 3.1 percent. Annual inflation increased from 3.7 percent in September to 3.8 percent in October. Energy prices rose just 0.7 percent in October, after jumping 5.4 percent in September. Although energy prices remain 22.4 percent higher than a year ago, they contributed relatively little to inflation in October, making it easier to assess underlying inflationary pressures. Core PCEPI, which excludes food and energy prices, rose 0.3 percent in October, the same as in September. Over the past three months, core prices have risen at an annualized rate of 3.6 percent. Annual core inflation increased from 3.1 percent in September to 3.3 percent in October, partly because core prices rose just 0.2 percent last October. Even so, recent monthly readings suggest that underlying inflation remains well above the Fed’s 2-percent target. The minutes of the Fed’s October meeting note that, according to Fed staff, “Total inflation was expected to step down sharply next year as energy prices decelerated.” Slower growth in energy prices would reduce headline inflation, but October’s core inflation figures suggest that it would not be enough to bring inflation back to target. The latest spending figures offer further reason for concern. Nominal spending, the dollar value of all final goods and services produced in the economy, grew at an annualized rate of 6.2 percent in the third quarter, according to the BEA’s second estimate, also released Wednesday.

items.title: Cautious consumers gear up for Black Friday as inflation woes bite By Reuters
items.excerpt: NEW YORK/LOS ANGELES, Nov 27 (Reuters) - Neither high fuel prices nor stubborn inflation are expected to stop US shoppers from spending robustly as their turkey hangovers wear off on Black Friday. But below healthy top-line forecasts lie signs of stress. Holiday spending — which unofficially begins on Black Friday — is seen topping last year’s strong figures by 4%-6%, several economic forecasts show. But most of the gains will be attributable to inflation which, at 3.8%, is about a percentage point higher than in each of the last two years.

items.title: US economy roars ahead in third quarter, inflation remains high in October By Reuters
items.excerpt: WASHINGTON, Nov 25 (Reuters) - The US economy grew much faster than initially estimated in the third quarter, while inflation increased further in October, reinforcing expectations that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates next month and again in early 2027. The sharp upward revision to gross domestic product last quarter, reported by the Commerce Department on Wednesday, marked the quickest economic growth pace in three years. It reflected upgrades to consumer spending and business investment, mostly related to artificial intelligence. Robust domestic demand is fueling inflation, with a measure of underlying price pressures in October posting its biggest year-over-year increase since late 2023. The economy has powered ahead despite the ongoing US-Israeli war with Iran.

items.excerpt: ## New on Netflix November 26: The Hunting Wives (Season 2) Now that we know who’s behind the death of Abby in The Hunting Wives, the show’s second season picks up after that reveal, with Margo (Malin Akerman) and her new pal Sophie (Brittany Snow) now estranged. They’ll be forced to come back together, though, as new secrets and mysteries pile up in the eight-episode season, which dropped Thanksgiving Day. ## New on Paramount+ November 26: The JLO Show The JLO Show is a concert film capturing the final night of Jennifer Lopez’s residency at Caesars Palace Las Vegas in 2025. The special concert event aired on CBS and Paramount+ on Thanksgiving night, but you can catch a special extended version on Paramount+ on demand today. ## New on Starz November 27: Outlander: Blood of My Blood season finale It’s time for the Twelfth Night masquerade party on Outlander: Blood of My Blood, the big event that will help close out season two of the Outlander prequel series. This season comes to a close on Friday, tune in and you can catch up on every other episode of the season on the Starz app.
